title: OpenWarrant Format 1.0: an authored record
description: Hand-written and normative for docs/format/FORMAT-1.0.md sections 3.4, 3.5, 3.6 and 5. Where this schema and the prose disagree, the prose wins and this schema is the defect. One record as a reader holds it after reading its heading `## <id> · <type> — <title>` and its attribute block: `fields` maps each field name to its value (continuations joined by LF, their first two spaces removed), `relations` lists each target of each relation line in order, and `body` is the text after the blank line. The bytes (separators, the blank line, continuation indentation, `format.attribute`, `format.field-duplicate`) are Appendix A's to describe. A section (`## <name>`) has no attribute block and is not described here.

type.description: A lowercase word or a dotted extension type (Appendix A `record-head`, section 7.2). The core types are `section`, `obligation`, `item`, `milestone`, `stage`, `warrant` and `ticket`; other undotted types come from the document's profile.

title.description: Section 3.4: REQUIRED, one line, at most 120 bytes (`format.title-missing`).

fields.description: Field name to value. A name is an undotted word the type or profile defines, or a dotted name (section 7).

relations.description: One entry per target of each relation line, in order of the lines.

to_revision.description: The `@sha256:<64 hex>` pin, when the target carries one.
